messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Horizontal distance (range) after a time \(t\)**  

For a projectile launched with speed \(v\) at an angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal, the horizontal component of the velocity is  

\[
v_x = v\cos\theta .
\]

Assuming no air resistance and a flat launch/landing surface, the horizontal distance travelled in a time \(t\) is simply

\[
\boxed{\,x(t)=v\cos\theta \; t\, } .
\]

---

**Vertical displacement after a time \(t\)**  

The vertical component of the velocity is \(v_y=v\sin\theta\).  
With gravitational acceleration \(g\approx9.81\;\text{m/s}^2\) (downward), the vertical position relative to the launch point is

\[
y(t)=v\sin\theta \; t-\frac12 g t^{2}.
\]

---

**Total path length after a time \(t\)**  

If you want the straight‑line distance from the launch point to the point reached after time \(t\) (ignoring curvature of the trajectory), you can combine the two components:

\[
s(t)=\sqrt{\bigl(v\cos\theta \; t\bigr)^{2}+\bigl(v\sin\theta \; t-\tfrac12 g t^{2}\bigr)^{2}} .
\]

---

### Quick example

Suppose a car is launched with \(v=20\;\text{m/s}\) at \(\theta=30^\circ\) and you want the horizontal distance after \(t=3\;\text{s}\):

\[
x(3)=20\cos30^\circ \times 3 \approx 20\times0.866\times3 \approx 51.96\;\text{m}.
\]

Feel free to plug in your own numbers for \(v\), \(\theta\), and \(t\) to get the distance.
